content:
Hello everybody!

My name is Marcus Collins. I'm a senior in high school in Los Angeles, but I've taken a number of undergrad math classes. My school has a program where students can study topics of their interest, and I'll be learning Lean this semester. I've finished the natural number game and am working through Mathematics in Lean. My end goal is to write up a formalization of Sharkovsky's theorem, a personal favorite of mine (I see this has been done before, and also the proof doesn't use anything too crazy, just some very clever applications of IVT), but I'm willing to pivot if this proves too hard.

One quick initial question - when I'm opening up a new file in the Math in Lean book, it takes a couple minutes for the Lean Infoview to load. Is this normal or does this mean it's compiling more than it has to?

Thanks so much. I'm so excited to learn with this community!

:grinning:

It's definitely not normal for me, but you and I might be in different situations. How much memory does your computer have? Have you got everything compiled? (i.e. what happens if you run lake build on the command line in the repo?) And do you have an antivirus on? (e.g. it once took about 45 seconds for Lean to start on any file on my computer, and after a lot of debugging it turned out that it was Microsoft Defender; when I switched it off everything started to work instantly).

If you have 8 or 4 gigs then that's probably the problem. If you have 16 or more then check all your files are compiled and temporary disable your antivirus to see if it makes a difference.

Thanks for the help. I'm on 8 gigs so I guess that's probably the reason, though turning off my antivirus seems to have helped a bit. Guess I'm due for an upgrade. :smiley: Lake build appears to be working normally, as far as I can tell (it outputs "Build completed successfully, 3438 jobs").
Yeah "Build completed successfully" is a good sign. I don't know if #mil has been modulized yet, that may help (but it may not).
I expect that would help --- but #mil has not been modulised yet. (In fact, I have an open PR to do this. I can ask the authors again.)

Thanks for the help. It's not too bad, just a few minutes.

What do you all think of the goal of Sharkovsky's theorem? Is it feasible for a beginner, and should I get to work after chapter 4 or is there more I should learn? Thanks again!
If you already understand the mathematics of the proof then I would just make a project and get going and see what happens. Doing a project is how everyone learnt lean in the pre-AI era.
Sounds good, I'll get started as soon as I finish up the function chapter. :)
